original_value: Expectation maximization (EM) algorithm is to find maximum likelihood solution for models having latent variables. A typical example is Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) which requires Gaussian assumption, however, natural images are highly non-Gaussian so that GMM cannot be applied to perform image clustering task on pixel space. To overcome such limitation, we propose a GAN based EM learning framework that can maximize the likelihood of images and estimate the latent variables. We call this model GAN-EM, which is a framework for image clustering, semi-supervised classification and dimensionality reduction. In M-step, we design a novel loss function for discriminator of GAN to perform maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) on data with soft class label assignments. Specifically, a conditional generator captures data distribution for K classes, and a discriminator tells whether a sample is real or fake for each class. Since our model is unsupervised, the class label of real data is regarded as latent variable, which is estimated by an additional network (E-net) in E-step. The proposed GAN-EM achieves state-of-the-art clustering and semi-supervised classification results on MNIST, SVHN and CelebA, as well as comparable quality of generated images to other recently developed generative models.

result.paraphrase: The expectation maximization (EM) algorithm seeks the maximum-likelihood solution for models with latent variables. A common case is the Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), which assumes Gaussianity; however, natural images are strongly non-Gaussian, so GMM cannot be used to carry out image clustering in pixel space. To address this limitation, we introduce a GAN-based EM learning framework that maximizes image likelihood and estimates latent variables. We refer to this model as GAN-EM, a framework for image clustering, semi-supervised classification, and dimensionality reduction. During the M-step, we devise a new loss function for the GAN discriminator to perform maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) on data with soft class-label assignments. In particular, a conditional generator models the data distribution for K classes, and a discriminator determines, for each class, whether a sample is real or fake. Because the model is unsupervised, the class label of real data is treated as a latent variable and is inferred by an auxiliary network (E-net) in the E-step. The proposed GAN-EM achieves state-of-the-art clustering and semi-supervised classification performance on MNIST, SVHN, and CelebA, while producing images of quality comparable to other recently developed generative models.
